question.prompt: Francesca uses \(100\) grams of lemon juice, \(100\) grams of sugar, and \(400\) grams of water to make lemonade. There are \(25\) calories in \(100\) grams of lemon juice and \(386\) calories in \(100\) grams of sugar. Water contains no calories. How many calories are in \(200\) grams of her lemonade?

solutions.explanation:
First find the mass and calories of the whole batch. Its mass is
\[
100+100+400=600\text{ grams},
\]
and its calorie total is \(25+386=411\), since water contributes none.

The batch makes three equal \(200\)-gram servings. Each serving of the mixed lemonade has one-third of the batch's calories, so it contains
\[
411\div3=137\text{ calories}.
\]
The answer is \(137\) calories, choice B.
solutions.title: Divide the batch into equal servings
